name: Crazy Solo
description: Crazy Solo (often just called 'Solo' in parts of Eastern Europe and USA) is a trick-taking card game for 3 to 12 players, though 4 is standard. It features a bidding hierarchy where players can 'Go Alone' (Solo) against the others. The game is known for its escalating bids involving specific trump suits (Hearts high) and partnership calling.

content.text: Crazy Solo (often just called 'Solo' in parts of Eastern Europe and USA) is a trick-taking card game for 3 to 12 players, though 4 is standard. It features a bidding hierarchy where players can 'Go Alone' (Solo) against the others. The game is known for its escalating bids involving specific trump suits (Hearts high) and partnership calling.
Derived from L'Hombre via Solo Whist, but with Americanized bidding rules (using Hearts as a premium suit).
Three to twelve players; four or more is standard.
36 cards (standard); 30, 32, 33 or 35 depending on player count.
36 cards (standard); 30, 32, 33 or 35 depending on player count.

All cards distributed one at a time starting with the player to the left of the dealer. With 4, 6, 9 or 12 players use full 36-card deck; with 5 or 7 remove six of spades (35); with 8 remove all sixes (32); with 10 remove all sixes plus seven of spades and seven of clubs (30); with 11 remove sixes of spades, clubs and diamonds (33). Player to dealer's left is on the lead.

items.text: Going Blind: Player on the lead may declare blind before looking at cards; if they have at least one heart they must go under (be solo) with Hearts as trump; no other player may bid. If no heart, hand reverts to normal bidding. Typically played once per evening.
Gang call-out: A gang player may call out that the gang is taking the trick to encourage others to dump point-cards; undiscovered partner may bluff by calling gang.
